text: LLM-based Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS) have demonstrated their potential indiverse educational scenarios by providing personalized and adaptive learning paths, tailored to the learner’scurrent needs [6, 8, 16, 17]. However, challenges such as the potential to offload academic work [18],insincere student responses [3] and biases in the training data of LLMs [11, 12] can lead to a lack of sustainedstudent engagement with LLM-PATs, which persists as a critical challenge [2, 19].Gamification strategies have been explored as an approach to enhance engagement and learning outcomesin various educational contexts [1, 15, 20]. Studies have demonstrated that game elements such as points,badges, or leaderboards can positively influence engagement [4, 21]. However, some studies also reportnegative effects of gamification on learning outcomes [4, 15], suggesting that its overall impact may not beuniversally positive and requires further investigation, particularly in the context of LLM-PATs.
